To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) partial knowledge of a previously experienced word–object mapping facilitates the learning of a subsequent, new mapping, and (2) this facilitation is due to the fact that partial knowledge can be used for disambigu-ating the meanings of new words.

partial knowledge of one word-object mapping accelerates the acquisition of both that mapping and other word-object mappings and that this acceleration is due to the ability of partial knowledge to disambiguate other word-object mappings even before the first mapping is learned.

(1) partial knowledge of a mapping accelerates the acquisition of other mappings, and (2) partial knowledge of some mappings accelerates the acquisition and disambiguation of other mappings even before the threshold is reached.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of partial knowledge of a single word in statistical learning and shows how partial knowledge of a few words can facilitate the acquisition of many others.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the learning of word meaning is an accumulative process that involves the accumulation of knowledge about individual mappings, and that partial knowledge of a mapping can speed the acquisition of other mappings.
partial knowledge of one word speeds up the learning of other words, and the mechanism underlying this effect is that of disambiguation.
the partial knowledge of some word–object mappings facilitates learning of other mappings by reducing the amount of information needed to reach the threshold of learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

partial knowledge of some word–object mappings can facilitate the acquisition of other mappings by providing information about the meaning of the word that can be used to disambiguate other word–object pairs, even before the threshold for learning is reached.
partial knowledge of a mapping can accelerate the learning of a new mapping, but the effect is more powerful when the learner is not yet committed to the old mapping.
the accumulation of partial information across multiple exposures to a word–object mapping is critical for learning, even if the mapping is not yet learned.
The main takeaway from our work is that
partial knowledge can be a valuable resource in learning, even when it is not enough to reach the threshold required for learning.
partial knowledge of one word’s meaning can be used to learn other words.
partial knowledge can have a significant impact on the learning process and that this impact may not always be obvious or immediate.
